pool:cms.summary: Cache the rates first. All 10 slots with the rates CMS were busy from about 160 visitors at once, and a short cache means almost no request needs a slot, so the limit stops mattering at the campaign's 260.

check_first.step: Check how quickly a rate change in the CMS has to show on the site.
check_first.reason: It sets the cache time: 30–60 seconds suits rates that change a few times a day; if an edit must show at once, clear the cache when rates are published.

ranked_fixes.fix: Cache the rates CMS's answers for a short time (for example 30–60 seconds), so most requests never need a slot.
ranked_fixes.reason: The CMS then gets one call per cache period, down from 35 a second, so the bottleneck goes away.

ranked_fixes.fix: Combine identical requests that are in flight at the same moment.
ranked_fixes.reason: When the cache expires during a busy second, the requests waiting for the new rates share one CMS call and leave the other slots free.

ranked_fixes.fix: When the CMS is slow, show the last rates it sent and refresh them in the background.
ranked_fixes.reason: Visitors at campaign peak keep seeing real rates when the CMS slows down for any reason, and on a savings page the rate is what they came for.

ranked_fixes.fix: On the server, drop queued requests whose visitor has already given up, so the slots go to people still waiting.
ranked_fixes.reason: Successful requests fell from 35/s to 10.8/s because slots went to answers nobody was waiting for; this keeps the throughput if a queue forms anyway.

ranked_fixes.fix: Keep the timeout and fallback for when it's slow anyway.
ranked_fixes.reason: It already works: visitors saw the fallback message during the collapse, so keep it as the safety net.

ranked_fixes.fix: Ask the provider for a higher limit.
ranked_fixes.reason: Last: it takes time and money and only moves the limit, and with caching 10 slots should be plenty.

db:findUserByEmail.summary: Confirm the full scan with the query plan, then add the index. It can wait, but it's a small change and the cost of each sign-up grows with the table.

check_first.step: Check the query plan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN) to confirm.
check_first.reason: Confidence is medium because the analyser only sees timings; SCAN in the plan confirms the full table scan.

ranked_fixes.fix: Add an index on the column the query looks up.
ranked_fixes.reason: The database then finds the row directly, so a lookup stays fast however many users sign up.

ranked_fixes.fix: Check that the query compares the email column directly (WHERE email = ?).
ranked_fixes.reason: Wrapping the column in LOWER() or matching with LIKE stops the database using the index, so the fix would quietly do nothing.

ranked_fixes.fix: Run the sign-up test again with about 10 times today's users in the table.
ranked_fixes.reason: The finding says it gets slower as the table grows; a bigger table shows how much the index saves before real data gets there.

render:SignupPage.summary: Cache the rendered page first. The page is the same for every visitor and its render took about 80% of the server's time, so caching removes most of the load in one change; profile it afterwards to make the first render faster.

check_first.step: Profile a single render (node --cpu-prof, or React DevTools' Profiler) and look at how many components the page renders and what each one does while rendering.
check_first.reason: It explains why one render takes about 14ms. Caching helps whatever the answer, so this can come second.

check_first.step: Check the query plan (EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN) for the email lookup.
check_first.reason: It confirms the full table scan before adding the index.

ranked_fixes.fix: Cache the rendered HTML (it's the same for every visitor), or generate it once at build time.
ranked_fixes.reason: At about 14ms a page the server can render only about 70 pages a second; a cached page costs almost nothing.

ranked_fixes.fix: Add an index on the column the query looks up, so the database finds the row directly.
ranked_fixes.reason: The email lookup is the next biggest share of the server's time (about 16%), and the change is small.

ranked_fixes.fix: Keep anything that differs per visitor (a form token, a name) out of the cached HTML, and load it separately.
ranked_fixes.reason: Otherwise the first visitor-specific change to the page would quietly turn the cache off.

ranked_fixes.fix: Simplify the component tree: fewer components, and no heavy work while rendering.
ranked_fixes.reason: Worth doing once profiling shows where the time goes, but with a cache it only speeds up the first render.

ranked_fixes.fix: If it has to stay dynamic, run several server processes (Node's cluster module) so renders don't all share one event loop.
ranked_fixes.reason: Last: it multiplies capacity by the number of cores but still pays for every render, and a cache makes it unnecessary.
